query: Plasmid reporter delivery into pluripotent stem cell-derived human cortical organoids by lumen microinjection followed by cuvette electroporation, with 24-hour fluorescence visualization and expression analysis in neural progenitors and their progeny
title: Injection and electroporation of plasmid DNA into human cortical organoids
markdown:
## Protocol: Plasmid reporter delivery into pluripotent stem cell-derived human cortical organoids by lumen microinjection followed by cuvette electroporation, with 24-hour fluorescence visualization and expression analysis in neural progenitors and their progeny

### Overview

This protocol details the delivery of plasmid reporters into pluripotent stem cell-derived human cortical organoids via lumen microinjection followed by cuvette electroporation. The process involves preparing specific reagents (organoid media, Fast Green dye, agarose), generating and purifying endotoxin-free plasmid DNA, and preparing glass injection needles. Organoids are cultured from H9 or H9-derived hESCs, loaded into an agarose furrow, injected with a plasmid-Fast Green mixture, collected, and subjected to electroporation using Program A-023. Transfection efficiency is assessed via fluorescence microscopy 1–5 days post-injection in neural progenitors and their progeny.

### Materials/Reagents

DMEM:F12 GlutaMAX, N-2 Supplement 1x, B-27 Supplement 1x, MEM Non-Essential AA 1x, beta-Mercaptoethanol, Anti-Anti 1x, Insulin (2.5 mg/mL), Fast Green powder, ddH2O, UltraPure Agarose, Qiagen EndoFree Plasmid Maxi Kit (or alternative EndoFree kit), Cell Line Nucleofector Solution V, DPBS, 70% Ethanol.

### Equipment

Microinjector, needle puller, microgrinder, light microscope, stereo microscope, P1000 pipettes (tips cut with razorblade), 20 µL Microloader pipette tips, hemocytometer, cuvettes, Nucleofector device (Program A-023), AggreWell plates, Eppendorf tubes, Petri dishes, razor blades, tweezers.

### Safety & Sterility

Prepare Fast Green powder under a chemical hood; wear gloves and lab coat to prevent inhalation and staining. Filter sterilize Fast Green solution. Clean workspace with ethanol before and after use. Use new or ethanol-cleaned razor blades to avoid contamination. Handle heated agarose carefully due to eruptive boiling risk; wear goggles. Ensure endotoxin-free plasmid DNA to maintain organoid survival. Keep organoids on the injection furrow for a maximum of 15 minutes. Discard injection furrows after one day of use to prevent contamination from media deposits.

## Reagent Preparation

### Organoid culturing media preparation

1. Prepare organoid culturing media by mixing 474.5 mL DMEM:F12 GlutaMAX, 5 mL N-2 Supplement 1x, 10 mL B-27 Supplement 1x, 5 mL MEM Non-Essential AA 1x, 0.5 mL beta-Mercaptoethanol, and 5 mL Anti-Anti 1x to reach a total volume of 500 mL. Mix, filter-sterilize, and store at 4°C for up to 1 month. Add fresh Insulin (2.5 mg/mL) immediately before use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->

### Fast Green solution preparation

1. 10 3 Fast Green solution

Reagent Final concentration Amount

Fast Green 1% 100 mg

ddH2O n/a 10 mL Total 10 mL

Storage at 4 C for up to 18 months

CRITICAL: Fast Green powder should be prepared under a chemical hood to prevent inha-
lation. Furthermore, wear gloves and lab coat to prevent green stains. Filter sterilize fast green solution before usage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Storage at 4 C for up to 18 months [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T1-S02 -->

### Agarose solution preparation

1. Prepare a 1% Agarose solution by dissolving 1 g UltraPure Agarose in 100 mL ddH2O. Use the solution immediately after preparation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T2-S01 -->

## Analysis

### 1-5 days post injection

1. Assess transfection efficiency using fluorescence microscopy of the electroporated organoids 1–5 days post-injection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S80 -->

## Procedure

### Grow cortical organoids

1. Select a starting cell line; here, H9 or H9-derived H3.1-miCOUNT hESCs are used. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Generate cortical organoids using the previously published protocol (Qian et al., 2018). Alterations may include using AggreWell plates to generate embryoid bodies from a fixed number of cells (Denoth-Lippuner et al., 2021). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: If both the starting cell line and the plasmid to be introduced express fluorescent proteins, ensure that their emission spectra are compatible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->

### Prepare DNA solution for injection

1. Generate plasmid DNA using the Qiagen EndoFree Plasmid Maxi Kit following the manufacturer's instructions, eluting the plasmid in ultrapure distilled water. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. Measure the concentration of the generated plasmid DNA. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Prepare an Eppendorf tube containing 18 mL of plasmid DNA solution with a total of 20 µg DNA per plasmid and condition. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
4. Add 2 mL of 10 3 Fast Green solution and mix by pipetting (alternative dye see materials andequipment). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->
5. Prepare one Eppendorf tube with 18 mL of H2O with 2 mL of 10 3 Fast Green solution to adjust injection conditions (Fast Green test solution). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Use an EndoFree Plasmid Kit to generate endotoxin-free plasmid DNA, as endotoxin-containing DNA may decrease the survival of injected and electroporated organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S06 -->

### Prepare organoid injection furrow

1. Prepare a 1% agarose solution in a flask or beaker. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. Heat the agarose solution in a microwave until it is completely dissolved. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->
3. Gently swirl the dissolved agarose solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->
4. Cool the agarose solution down to 55°C–60°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S04 -->
5. Pour the cooled agarose solution into a Petri dish, ensuring an agarose layer thickness of 1–2 cm. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S05 -->
6. Allow the agarose to solidify at 23°C or 4°C (the latter is faster). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S06 -->
7. Use a razor blade to cut an agarose furrow approximately 1 cm wide, 1 cm deep, and 6 cm long, as shown in Figures 1A and 1E. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S07 -->
8. Use the agarose plate immediately or seal it with parafilm and store at 4°C for later use. Always ensure the agarose is completely cooled down before handling. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S08 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Clean the working space with ethanol and use a new or ethanol-cleaned razor blade to avoid contaminations. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Carefully handle the agarose solution after microwave heating due to the high risk of eruptive boiling; wear goggles to protect your eyes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S10 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: The furrow should not be too deep, otherwise the needle might not reach the organoids. Several furrows can be cut into one agarose plate to find the ideal depth. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S11 -->

### Prepare injection needle

1. Pull needles from glass capillaries using a needle puller, keeping the parameters consistent between experiments. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. Cut the pulled needle with tweezers. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->
3. Grind the needle tip using a microgrinder at a 45° angle until the desired tip size with smooth edges is achieved. Confirm the thickness, shape, and quality of the needle tip with a light microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->
4. Wash needles with 70% Ethanol followed by DPBS washes before first use and for reuse. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: To minimize damage to the organoid during injection, the needle tip should be small and sharp. However, if the tip is too small, it may clog with tissue; grind longer to increase tip size if clogging occurs. If the tip is too big, liquid may leak out, causing excessive tissue damage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S05 -->

### Prepare workspace

1. Prepare labeled Eppendorf tubes for transporting the organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
2. Turn on the microinjector, allowing several minutes for calibration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->
3. Prepare cuvettes and set the Nucleofector device to Program A-023. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S03 -->
4. Cut off the tips of several P1000 pipette tips with a razorblade to facilitate the transfer of organoids. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Microinjections and electroporations can be performed outside the cell culture hood, but clean the workspace with 70% Ethanol before and after use to minimize contaminations. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: The tip size of the cut-off P1000 depends on the size of the organoids. If the opening is too big, pipetting small volumes is difficult; if too small, organoids might be damaged. Always pre-wet the pipette tip before handling organoids to prevent them from sticking to the inside walls. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S06 -->

### Prepare media

1. Prewarm (23°C) Eppendorf tubes containing 100 µL of Cell Line Nucleofector Solution V. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->
2. Prepare 3 mL of fresh media to collect organoids and fresh media to feed organoids immediately after electroporation, warming both to 37°C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S02 -->
3. Prepare 1 collection 6-well plate containing 3 mL of media per well, kept in a 37°C incubator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S03 -->

### Needle loading and adjustment of injection settings

1. Take the prepared glass needle. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S01 -->
2. Fill the needle with 10 µL of the Fast Green test solution using 20 µL Microloader pipette tips. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S02 -->
3. Insert the filled needle into the capillary holder. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S03 -->
4. Set initial injection parameters: 45 hPa injection pressure (pi), 0.14 s injection time (ti), and 0 hPa compensation pressure (pc). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S04 -->
5. Eject a drop of the solution onto a hemocytometer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S05 -->
6. Adjust settings to generate a drop with approximately 250 µm radius, corresponding to approximately 65 nL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S06 -->
7. Eject the H2O solution containing Fast Green onto paper tissue by pressing ‘clean' for several seconds. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S07 -->
8. Reload the needle with the plasmid DNA solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S08 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Before cleaning the needle, ensure it is properly screwed into the capillary holder to prevent ejecting the needle. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: These calibration steps are essential and must be repeated every time the glass needle is changed. To increase drop size, increase pi or ti, but keep pi relatively low to prevent organoid damage. If the needle tip dries and blocks, pc can be increased, but high pc will result in a constant flow of plasmid DNA. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T6-S10 -->

### Load organoids into injection furrow

1. Collect organoids using a cut-off P1000 tip. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S01 -->
2. Distribute 10–20 organoids along the injection furrow. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S02 -->
3. Remove some excess media using an uncut P1000 or P200 pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S03 -->
4. Place the plate containing organoids under the stereo microscope. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Organoids should be half-covered and surrounded by media to prevent drying out, but not fully covered, to keep them stable during injections. Avoid injecting more than 20 organoids at a time. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T7-S05 -->

### Inject organoids

1. Gently push the needle into the center of the organoid. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S01 -->
2. Push the ‘inject' key. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S02 -->
3. Gently pull out the needle. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S03 -->
4. Repeat the injection process until the green DNA solution is clearly visible inside the organoid. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S04 -->
5. Move to the next organoid in the row. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: The organoid should be filled with green plasmid DNA solution. If the solution flows out, the needle was not placed correctly or the injection volume needs adjustment (lower pi or ti). If no DNA is ejected, the needle might be clogged or dried out. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Avoid inserting the needle into the agarose, as it might break or clog. Equally, avoid perforating through the organoid, as this causes leakiness of the plasmid solution and disrupts tissue integrity. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S07 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: The time organoids spend on the injection furrow should be kept to a minimum (max 15 min). Inexperienced experimenters should start with low numbers of organoids injected at once. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T8-S08 -->

### Collect organoids from injection furrow

1. Flush organoids out of the injection furrow with DPBS using the P1000 with a cut-off tip. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S01 -->
2. Transfer the flushed organoids into an Eppendorf tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S02 -->
3. Remove as much DPBS as possible from the tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S03 -->
4. Clean the injection furrow with DPBS for immediate reuse. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S04 -->
5. Note: Carefully check by eye that all organoids are collected from the injection plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: The injection furrow should be discarded after a full day of usage, as cell culture media deposits may become contaminated and cause issues during further injections. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T9-S06 -->

### Electroporate organoids

1. Add 100 µL of prewarmed (23°C) nucleofector solution to the organoids in the Eppendorf tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S01 -->
2. b. Transfer whole solution containing organoids from the Eppendorf tube to the cuvette (problem 3). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S02 -->
3. Electroporate the organoids using program A-023. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S03 -->
4. Add 1 mL of prewarmed media into the cuvette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S04 -->
5. Flush out the organoids by pouring the cuvette contents into the prepared collection 6-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S05 -->
6. Repeat flushing until all organoids are transferred to the collection 6-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S06 -->
7. Collect the organoids and transfer them back to the original well to remove excess debris and dissociated tissue resulting from injection and electroporation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S07 -->
8. Add fresh media for further culturing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S08 -->
9. i. Assess transfection at selected time points using method of choice (problem 5). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S09 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Do not overfill the electroporation cuvette with nucleofector solution; the solution containing organoids should not exceed the limit of the paddle, as more than 100 µL will trigger an error message from the electroporator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S10 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Flush out organoids carefully from the cuvette to prevent damaging fragile organoids post-electroporation. Try to keep the number of organoids inside the cuvette consistent between experiments to reduce variability. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S11 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: Electroporation should be executed as fast as possible to prevent diffusion of plasmids out of the organoids and to minimize the time organoids spend outside the incubator. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T10-S12 -->
